q: When index r enters a window of size k, which index leaves?
why: The new window is [r − k + 1, r], so the element at r − k just dropped out.

q: Max sum over all windows of size k using a sliding sum costs…
why: One O(k) setup and then O(1) per slide for n − k slides.

q: What is best for nums = [1, 4, 2, 10, 2, 3], k = 2?
code:
s = best = sum(nums[:k])
for r in range(k, len(nums)):
    s += nums[r] - nums[r - k]
    best = max(best, s)
why: Window sums are 5, 6, 12, 12, 5. The best is 12.

q: "Does s2 contain a permutation of s1?" What should the window hold?
options: A sorted copy of the window
why: A permutation has the same letter counts. Compare two 26-slot arrays as the window slides.

q: Contains Duplicate II keeps a set of the last k values. When is a value removed?
options: When the set holds more than k values: remove nums[i − k]
why: The set must only hold values within distance k of the current index.

q: Maximum average of a length-k window: what do you track?
options: The maximum sum; divide by k once at the end
why: All windows have the same length, so the largest sum gives the largest average. Dividing once avoids float noise.
